# Pavel Guzhikov

> Pavel Guzhikov builds and runs companies. London-based. Zero to one, four times. Two exits. One unicorn: founding team at Uzum, Uzbekistan's first unicorn. guzh.uk is Pavel Guzhikov's personal site, and also carries the privacy policy, help and ideas pages for Always Weather, a weather app (paid in the app stores, free on Linux) whose own home is alwaysweather.uk, and the pages for Always Today, a to-do list app (free on one device, with paid sync; a download for Mac and Linux, in review at Google Play for Android and out there in a few days, with iPhone, iPad and Windows coming soon). It also carries the page and the privacy policy for Goat Rodeo, a party game on Google Play.

Twenty years of building, from a multi-channel mobile messenger in 2005 to national payment infrastructure in 2022.

- Uzum: founding team. Fintech, lending, marketplace, payments, cards, and the data culture underneath them. Millions of users and 1000+ employees in two years, in a market with no digital infrastructure.
- Before that: founded and sold Worki, Russia's fastest-growing jobs marketplace (acquired by Mail.Ru Group, 2019). Co-founded Dengi Vpered, earned-wage access backed by Target Global (sold). Fintech products with 100+ banks.
- Now: most interested in problems where the technology is genuinely hard, the deployment is political and the blast radius is national: sovereign infrastructure, public systems, defence and dual-use, AI in the public interest.
- Building now: [Agent Hands](https://agenthands.cc/), which lets any AI hire a person nearby for a real-world task. The money is locked before anyone sees the task and paid in USDC once the proof is accepted.
- Building now, too: [Ruminator.xyz](https://ruminator.xyz/), for anyone who needs to know what is really happening inside Russia, and what Russians are told about it, beyond Moscow's national channels: journalists, analysts, researchers, diplomats, investors. Every day it reads Russia's regional and local press, from state television to independent and exiled outlets and residents' Telegram channels, across dozens of regions, and shows what each kind of outlet reports, how it frames it and what it steers readers towards. Every claim is checked word for word against the source, and members can ask an AI journalist questions answered from the articles. Invite-only: request access at https://ruminator.xyz/request-access, then £19 a month or £182.40 a year.
- Also building, as a citizen: [LedgerGov.UK](https://ledgergov.uk/), an open P&L of the UK state that shows where public money comes from, where it goes and what every political promise would cost, with each number linked to its official source. And [BoroughBook.UK](https://boroughbook.uk/), the same idea for one London borough: where your council tax goes in Hammersmith & Fulham, the council's budget, both parties' pledges and every payment over £500. Both are independent public alphas.

Contact: pavel@guzh.uk

## Pages

- [Pavel Guzhikov](https://guzh.uk/): the home page. Background, track record, current focus and contact details.
- [Always Weather](https://alwaysweather.uk/): a calm weather app for iPhone, Apple Watch and Mac (App Store), Android phones, Pixel Watch and Googlebooks (Google Play) and Windows PCs (Microsoft Store), paid once in each store, and free on Linux (made on Omarchy, for Arch systems, with a line in Omarchy's bar; one-command install from the page). Drag your thumb through the hours to see exactly when the rain starts and stops. Ten days ahead, up to ten saved places. No subscription, no ads, no account, no tracking.
- [Always Weather privacy policy](https://guzh.uk/weather/privacy/): the app's privacy policy. Location only if you choose it, rounded to about a kilometre before it leaves the device; saved places and settings stay on the device.
- [Always Weather help and contact](https://guzh.uk/weather/support/): help with the app. Email apps@guzh.uk.
- [Suggest an idea for Always Weather](https://guzh.uk/weather/ideas/): a short form that sends an idea for the app straight to the person who makes it. No account; an email address only if you would like an answer.
- [Always Today](https://alwaystoday.uk/): a calm, local-first to-do list that answers one question every morning: what am I doing today? Out now as a download for Macs with Apple silicon (https://alwaystoday.uk/download/mac) and as a fast terminal app for Linux, made on Omarchy (https://alwaystoday.uk/release/linux-terminal), and as a window app for Linux desktops (https://alwaystoday.uk/release/linux-desktop). The Android app, for phones and Googlebooks, is in review at Google Play, the iPhone and iPad app at the App Store, and the Windows app at the Microsoft Store; each is out in a few days. Works offline; plain-English quick entry ("call bank tomorrow 3pm #admin"); optional end-to-end encryption; import from Things, Todoist and TickTick. Free on one device, for ever. Sync between devices costs £24 a year or £3 a month, or £59 once for Lifetime, with 7 days free and no card needed. Sold through Google Play on Android, and by Stripe (shown as Onelink) on the web for Windows, Mac and Linux. No ads, no analytics, no tracking.
- [Always Today privacy policy](https://guzh.uk/today/privacy/): what the sync server keeps (email, devices and changes, encrypted if you choose), what never leaves the device, payments through Stripe and Google Play, and how long anything is kept.
- [Always Today help, contact and refunds](https://guzh.uk/today/support/): refunds within 14 days, no questions asked; plans and cancelling; common questions. Email apps@guzh.uk.
- [Always Today terms of use](https://guzh.uk/today/terms/): the terms for the app and its sync service, in plain English, under the law of England and Wales.
- [Goat Rodeo](https://guzh.uk/goat-rodeo/): a party platformer for Android phones, tablets and Chromebooks, on Google Play. One to four people on one device (one screen, or pass the phone), with bots for empty seats: each round everyone places an item in the level (planks, springs, saws, crossbows, a wrecking ball), then everyone races to the flag; you score when you reach it and your friends don't. Four levels free (Meadow, Canyon, Rooftops, Pumpkin Hollow); Full Rodeo, £2.99 once, adds nine more. Easy controls for younger players, a short video of each round's best moment to share. No ads, no account, plays offline; anonymous play counts only with the player's yes. Rated PEGI 7, ESRB Everyone.
- [Goat Rodeo privacy policy](https://guzh.uk/goat-rodeo/privacy/): the privacy policy for Goat Rodeo, where friends build a trap course together and then race through it. Four levels are free; Full Rodeo, a one-time purchase through Google Play, unlocks nine more. The game collects nothing about you: no ads, no account, no crash reports, no tracking; anonymous play counts (levels, items, how rounds end) only if the player says yes.
